_note: Hand-curated, source-read ICB emollient and over-the-counter positions for the ICB pack tool (app/icb-pack.js). One entry per ICB, only where read at source. Every entry carries its sources and the date it was read. Wording is paraphrased; add a short quote only if under 15 words. An ICB with no entry reads Not verified in the tool. Merged into data/icb-pack/index.json by scripts/build_icb_pack.py.

points: Self-care policy: a prescription for a medicine bought over the counter for mild dry skin should not routinely be offered in primary care, and patients with mild dry skin can manage long term on over-the-counter products.

If a clinician still prescribes (a general over-the-counter exclusion or individual patient needs), the policy lists the products to use: creams including Cetraben, Epimax, Hydromol, ZeroAQS and Zerocream; Doublebase gel; ointments including Epaderm, Hydromol and Zeroderm. Aveeno cream is listed for paediatric use only.

Formulary decision, 8 May 2025: Aproderm, Epimax and Zero emollient ranges approved as Green. Epaderm and Hydromol stay Green but are marked less cost-effective, for use when other options are unsuitable. Removal of Aveeno was confirmed with University Hospitals Birmingham dermatology, paediatrics and oncology. Changes go out through a primary care script switch.

The minutes say patients with mild dry skin should be encouraged to self-manage under the ICB policy on items not routinely prescribed, and that emollients with active ingredients such as urea or antimicrobials would be reviewed over the following months.
QV does not appear in either document (searched the text of both).
